cues.s1|Deformation gradient: F maps arrows: dx = F dX. Identity plus displacement gradient. J is the volume ratio, positive so matter keeps its handedness.
cues.s1|Cauchy-Green tensors: C = FᵀF sits on the reference side (Fᵀ first), B = FFᵀ on the current side. Squared stretch: λ² = N·CN.
cues.s1|Green-Lagrange strain: Half of (C − I), the squared length change. C = (I + H)ᵀ(I + H) expands to I + H + Hᵀ + HᵀH.
cues.s1|Small strain and rotation: Split the gradient: symmetric half is strain, skew half is rotation. Add them back and recover ∇u.
cues.s1|Polar decomposition: Read right to left: RU stretches then rotates, VR rotates then stretches. U² = C, V² = B, and V = RURᵀ.
cues.s1|2D strain compatibility: Each normal strain is differentiated twice across the other axis; shear on the right with factor 2, which equals ∂²γ₁₂/∂x₁∂x₂.
cues.s2|Cauchy's theorem: Traction equals stress times normal: t = σn, normal index contracted on j. Dot with n again for the normal stress.
cues.s2|Equilibrium and symmetry: Divergence of stress plus body force sums to zero (static Newton). Angular momentum makes σ symmetric.
cues.s2|Plane principal stresses: Mohr circle: centre at the mean (σ_x + σ_y)/2, radius √(half-difference² + τ²). Angles double on the circle.
cues.s2|Invariants and characteristic equatio: Signs alternate: s³ − I₁s² + I₂s − I₃. In principal values: sum, sum of pair products, product.
cues.s2|Von Mises stress: Root of half the sum of squared principal differences. Uniaxial check: σ₁ = σ gives ½(σ² + σ²), so σ_vm = σ.
cues.s2|Objectivity of Cauchy stress: Rotate the observer and stress is sandwiched: QσQᵀ. The response function obeys the same sandwich when F becomes QF.
cues.s3|Generalized Hooke's law: Fourth-order C eats two strain indices kl and returns two stress indices ij. Indices balance on both sides.
cues.s3|Isotropic stiffness form: Volume part λ tr ε on the identity, shear part 2με. The 2 matches τ = Gγ = 2Gε.
cues.s3|Isotropic compliance form: (1 + ν)/E on σ, minus ν/E times the trace. Uniaxial check: ε₁₁ = σ/E, ε₂₂ = −νσ/E.
cues.s3|Elastic constant relations: G pairs with 2(1 + ν), K with 3(1 − 2ν). λ shares the product (1 + ν)(1 − 2ν) in its denominator.
cues.s3|Plane stress stiffness: Prefactor E/(1 − ν²). Shear entry (1 − ν)/2 times γ gives Gγ, since E(1 − ν)/(2(1 − ν²)) = E/(2(1 + ν)).
cues.s3|Strain energy density: Half stress times strain, like ½kx². Differentiate W by ε to recover σ = λ(tr ε)I + 2με.
cues.s4|Airy stress function: Each normal stress differentiates twice along the other coordinate: σ_xx from ∂y², σ_yy from ∂x². Shear carries the minus sign.
cues.s4|Biharmonic equation: Laplacian of the Laplacian: coefficients 1, 2, 1, like (a + b)². It is the compatibility equation in φ.
cues.s4|Airy function in polar coordinates: σ_θθ is the plain second r-derivative. σ_rr adds (1/r)φ_r and (1/r²)φ_θθ. Shear: minus ∂/∂r of (1/r)φ_θ.
cues.s4|Plane strain out-of-plane stress: Set ε_zz = 0 in the compliance: σ_zz carries ν times the in-plane sum. At ν = ½ it equals their mean.
cues.s4|Plane stress to plane strain conversi: Plane strain is stiffer: E grows to E/(1 − ν²) and ν grows to ν/(1 − ν).
cues.s4|Kirsch hole solution: θ from the load axis: σ₀(1 − 2cos 2θ). At θ = 90° gives 3σ₀; at θ = 0 gives −σ₀.
cues.s5|Thin-walled cylinder: Hoop is twice axial: pr/t against pr/(2t). Diameter cut for hoop, cross cut for axial.
cues.s5|Thin-walled sphere: Every great circle cut looks alike: pr/(2t) in all tangent directions, equal to the cylinder's axial stress.
cues.s5|Lamé solution (cylinder): A ± B/r²: radial takes minus, hoop takes plus. The sum σ_rr + σ_θθ = 2A is constant through the wall.
cues.s5|Thick cylinder, internal pressure: Common factor pa²/(b² − a²). Checks: r = a gives σ_rr = −p, r = b gives σ_rr = 0.
cues.s5|Closed-end axial stress: End cap force pπa² spread over wall area π(b² − a²). It equals the Lamé constant A.
cues.s5|Thick sphere: Sphere uses 1/r³ with half the coefficient on the hoop term. Check with dσ_rr/dr + 2(σ_rr − σ_θθ)/r = 0.
cues.s12|Hyperelastic stresses: S = ∂W/∂E = 2∂W/∂C because E = ½(C − I). P = FS pushes one leg forward.
cues.s12|Stress measure conversions: P = JσF⁻ᵀ follows Nanson's area map. S = F⁻¹P is fully pulled back. Divide by J to return to σ.
cues.s12|Invariants of C: Same pattern as stress invariants: trace, half the trace-squared difference, determinant. det C = (det F)² = J².
cues.s12|Incompressible neo-Hookean: Energy grows with I₁ − 3, zero at the identity. Cauchy stress: −p on the identity plus μ times B.
cues.s12|Mooney-Rivlin: Neo-Hookean plus a C₂(I₂ − 3) term. Small strain shear modulus μ = 2(C₁ + C₂).
cues.s12|Neo-Hookean uniaxial tension: Free sides give p = μ/λ, so σ = μ(λ² − 1/λ); divide by λ for nominal P. Small strain: 3με = Eε.
cues.s13|Material time derivative: Ride the particle: local rate ∂/∂t plus convection v·∇. Steady flow still accelerates through the convective term.
cues.s13|Velocity gradient: L = ḞF⁻¹ pushes the rate forward. Symmetric part D stretches, skew part W spins. J̇/J = tr L = div v.
cues.s13|Conservation of mass: Net outflow from a fixed box drains its density. Following the particle, ρJ = ρ₀ stays constant.
cues.s13|Reynolds transport theorem: Moving region: material rate of φ plus φ times the volume growth rate div v.
cues.s13|Linear momentum balance: Newton per unit volume: div σ + b = ρa in current form; capital Div P + b₀ = ρ₀a in reference form.
cues.s13|Energy balance (first law): Internal energy rises by stress power σ:D, heat flowing in (−div q), and heat sources ρr.
cues.s15|Thermoelastic Hooke's law: Compliance adds αΔT I. Stiffness subtracts C:(αΔT I) = (3λ + 2μ)αΔT I = 3KαΔT I.
cues.s15|Restrained thermal stress: Heated and held means compression. Each restrained direction raises it: 1 for a bar, 1/(1 − ν) for a plate.
cues.s15|Rule of mixtures: Fibres side by side share strain: parallel springs, stiffnesses add. Phases in series share stress: compliances add.
cues.s15|Orthotropic reciprocity: Symmetric compliance: S₁₂ = −ν₁₂/E₁ = −ν₂₁/E₂. Loading along the stiff axis gives the larger ratio: E₁ > E₂ means ν₁₂ > ν₂₁.
cues.s15|Reduced stiffness of a ply: Common denominator 1 − ν₁₂ν₂₁; isotropic check gives E/(1 − ν²). ν₁₂E₂ = ν₂₁E₁ in Q₁₂; Q₆₆ = G₁₂.
cues.s15|ABD laminate relation: Through-thickness weights 1, z, z²: A in-plane, B coupling, D bending. A symmetric laminate has B = 0.
